name: Historic Centre of Sheki with the Khan’s Palace
description: Sheki is a mountain-foothill town in northwestern Azerbaijan, split in two by the Gurjana River and rebuilt in the 18th century after mudflows wiped out its predecessor. Its streets are lined with houses with steep gabled roofs. The highlight is the Khan's Palace of 1797, a summer residence, alongside merchant houses built on the fortunes of the silk-cocoon trade.
